raw_response:
I have been doing this for 60 years. My father did it before me. I do not need anyone to tell me what to plant — I know what this land wants.

My 10.2 mu: I put 8 mu into wheat and maize. Same ground, winter to summer, summer to winter. The other 2.2 mu I switched to stevia three years ago. Old Li next door put in stevia first and made better money than grain. So I followed him.

---

**Wheat (winter):**
I rotary till before planting. I put down one full bag of the 45 compound fertilizer per mu — that is 50 jin — mixed into the soil. Then in spring, when the wheat is about knee high and jointing, I broadcast urea. I do about 30 jin per mu of urea. That is what Old Zhang does and his wheat stands straight every year. I water three times: one winter water before the ground freezes, one at jointing, one when the grain is filling. Three waters — that is standard here. If it rains well I might skip the third but usually I do all three, I do not want to risk it. I spray once for aphids in spring and once for weeds early on. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe 480 if the season is good.

**Maize (summer):**
Right after wheat harvest I go back into the field the same day or next day. No plowing — I just plant into the stubble with the seeder. The hybrid seed from the village shop, same brand I used last three years. I put a small amount of compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, maybe 20 jin per mu. Then at the big-bell-mouth stage — when the stalk is chest height — I broadcast urea, about 40 jin per mu. Maize drinks a lot. Two waters: one at planting if dry, one at silking. If the summer rains are good I might do only one. I spray once or twice — mainly for corn borer and a bit of herbicide early. I expect 550 jin per mu, that is normal for here.

**Stevia:**
This one I still watch Old Li closely. He says stevia pulls a lot from the soil because you cut it three times in a year. So I put more fertilizer than on wheat. I do rotary tillage in spring before transplanting the cuttings. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at the start, then after each cut I add 15 jin of urea per mu to push regrowth. Stevia needs water more often — I water maybe five times through the season. I spray twice for bugs. Dry leaf I expect 130 jin per mu for the whole year across all three cuts. The price makes it worth the extra work.

My big worry is fertilizer cost. Last year the price went up. Two people, 10 mu, I cannot waste money. But I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than watch the yield drop and have nothing to sell. A bad harvest hurts the whole household.
